ep01-claude-code-best-ai-tool.title: Claude Code is the Best AI Tool on the Planet
ep01-claude-code-best-ai-tool.description: We explore why Claude Code with ChatGPT 5.5 is being called literally magic — from throwing complex tasks at it to getting polished results. A hands-on look at what happens when you combine two of the most powerful AI tools available.

ep02-jane-street-ai-hire.title: Jane Street Hired This Junior at $600K Because He Uses AI
ep02-jane-street-ai-hire.description: The story of how a junior developer landed a $220K to $600K per year role at Jane Street, one of the most prestigious trading firms in the world, primarily because of their AI skills. What this tells us about the changing job market.

ep03-energy-crisis-investing.title: Critical Commodity Shortages: How to Invest in an Energy Crisis
ep03-energy-crisis-investing.description: A deep dive into the coming commodity supercycle and why critical mineral shortages could reshape global energy markets. What the smart money is doing and where the opportunities lie.

ep04-codex-five-new-features.title: Codex 0.129.0: 5 New Features You Need to Know
ep04-codex-five-new-features.description: A walkthrough of the five most important new features in Codex 0.129.0 — from keymap debugging to Vim mode, raw mode, and the redesigned session browser. Essential listening for any Codex user.

ep05-izmir-real-estate-investment.title: I Made a Real Estate Investment in Izmir, Turkey
ep05-izmir-real-estate-investment.description: A firsthand look at buying property in Izmir, Turkey — from the process and prices to the realities of investing in Turkish real estate as a foreigner. What to expect, what to avoid, and why Izmir specifically.

ep06-cheap-residency-balkans.title: Albania, Serbia, and Montenegro: Cheap Residency Options
ep06-cheap-residency-balkans.description: Three Balkan countries are offering some of the easiest and cheapest residency pathways in Europe. We break down the requirements, costs, and lifestyle trade-offs for each option.

ep07-eu-bans-citizenship-investment.title: EU Banned Citizenship by Investment — Here's What Happened
ep07-eu-bans-citizenship-investment.description: The EU Court of Justice struck down formal citizenship-by-investment programmes in 2025. But demand hasn't disappeared — it's gone underground into discretionary 'citizenship by merit' schemes that operate with zero EU oversight.

ep08-anthropic-ai-company-blueprint.title: Anthropic's Official Blueprint for Building a Company With AI
ep08-anthropic-ai-company-blueprint.description: Anthropic published their official guide for building a company using AI agents. We break down the key strategies, architecture decisions, and practical advice from the team behind Claude.

ep09-anthropic-company-playbook.title: Anthropic's Official Playbook for Building an AI Company
ep09-anthropic-company-playbook.description: A companion to the blueprint — this episode covers the operational playbook: team structure, agent design patterns, and how to actually ship AI-powered products at scale.

ep10-open-source-software-factory.title: I Built My Own Software Factory and Open-Sourced It
ep10-open-source-software-factory.description: Matt Pocock built a complete software factory using AI agents and open-sourced the whole thing. We explore the architecture, the tooling choices, and what it means for solo developers.

ep11-nine-things-claude-code.title: 9 Things the Creator of Claude Code Wants You to Know
ep11-nine-things-claude-code.description: Boris Cherny, the creator of Claude Code at Anthropic, listed nine insights about how to get the most out of AI coding tools. From workflow patterns to mental models that change how you think about AI assistance.

ep12-karpathy-end-of-programming.title: Andrej Karpathy Just Declared the End of Programming
ep12-karpathy-end-of-programming.description: Andrej Karpathy — one of the founding minds of modern AI — says programming as we know it is over. Not clickbait, but a nuanced argument about how AI is fundamentally changing what it means to write code.

ep13-europe-tax-system-you-cant-escape.title: How Europe Is Designing a Tax System You Can't Escape
ep13-europe-tax-system-you-cant-escape.description: A look at how European countries, led by the Netherlands, are building an increasingly coordinated tax net that makes it harder than ever to optimise or reduce your tax burden legally.

ep14-istanbul-citizenship-real-estate.title: Secondhand Real Estate in Istanbul for Turkish Citizenship
ep14-istanbul-citizenship-real-estate.description: Buying secondhand property in Istanbul is one of the most popular routes to Turkish citizenship. We cover the process, the neighbourhoods, the pitfalls, and what your money actually buys you.

ep15-ten-hermes-agent-features.title: 10 Hermes Agent Features Most People Aren't Using
ep15-ten-hermes-agent-features.description: Hermes Agent is packed with features that most users never discover. From advanced tool configuration to memory management and multi-platform messaging — ten features that will change how you use AI agents.

ep16-istanbul-apartment-tour.title: We Toured 4 Istanbul Apartments for Turkish Citizenship
ep16-istanbul-apartment-tour.description: A tour of four actual apartments in central Istanbul that qualify for the Turkish citizenship by investment programme. Real prices, real neighbourhoods, and honest assessments of each property.

ep17-how-to-use-openai-code.title: How to Actually Use OpenAI Code — From the Engineers Who Built It
ep17-how-to-use-openai-code.description: OpenAI's own engineers showed how they actually use their own coding tools internally. Spoiler: it's not how you think. Practical tips and workflows straight from the team building the tools.

ep18-inside-communist-cuba.title: Inside Communist-Controlled Cuba's Humanitarian Crisis
ep18-inside-communist-cuba.description: Cuba is facing its largest humanitarian crisis in decades. We go inside the communist-controlled island to understand what's really happening — the food shortages, the power grid failures, the mass emigration, and why the system is finally buckling.

ep19-llms-hallucinate-lot.title: LLMs Hallucinate. A LOT. — Matt Pocock
ep19-llms-hallucinate-lot.description: Matt Pocock breaks down one of the most frustrating realities of working with AI: large language models hallucinate constantly. Why it happens, how to mitigate it, and whether it's a solvable problem or an inherent limitation we just have to live with.

ep20-hermes-agent-setup-step-step.title: Hermes Agent Setup: A Step-by-Step Guide
ep20-hermes-agent-setup-step-step.description: A complete walkthrough of setting up Hermes Agent from scratch. Installation, configuration, connecting to messaging platforms, and getting your first AI agent running — explained clearly and step by step.

ep21-video-thereluctantaccountant.title: AI Agents Are Changing Everything — Even Accounting
ep21-video-thereluctantaccountant.description: A look at how AI agents are disrupting traditional industries like accounting, and what it means for professionals who've spent decades building their careers.

ep22-stephanie-zhan-karpathy-i-are-back-.title: Karpathy's Software 3.0 Vision at Sequoia AI Ascent
ep22-stephanie-zhan-karpathy-i-are-back-.description: Andrej Karpathy returns to Sequoia's AI Ascent to explain Software 3.0 — where prompting replaces programming, vibe coding raises the floor, and agentic engineering raises the ceiling.

ep23-sarah-guo-caught-up-karpathy-new-no.title: Karpathy on No Priors: The Phase Shift in AI
ep23-sarah-guo-caught-up-karpathy-new-no.description: Andrej Karpathy joins the No Priors podcast to discuss the phase shift happening in AI right now — from how models are trained to how they're changing software development and society.

ep24-movez-jane-street-ai-engineer-revea.title: How Jane Street Uses AI to Hire Engineers
ep24-movez-jane-street-ai-engineer-revea.description: A Jane Street engineer reveals how the elite trading firm uses AI skills as a hiring signal — and what it takes to land a $600K role straight out of school.

ep25-mnimiy-karpathy-threw-grenade-at-ev.title: Karpathy Threw a Grenade at Every Senior Engineer
ep25-mnimiy-karpathy-threw-grenade-at-ev.description: Andrej Karpathy's latest take on AI coding has senior engineers rattled. He argues that vibe coding isn't just for beginners — it's the future of all software development.

ep26-cyrilxbt-instead-spending-weeks-fig.title: I Spent Tonight Figuring Out Codex So You Don't Have To
ep26-cyrilxbt-instead-spending-weeks-fig.description: A deep dive into OpenAI's Codex coding agent — setting it up, figuring out the workflow, and discovering what it actually does well (and where it falls apart).

ep27-bio-hack-gut-health.title: The Bio Hack Revolution: Gut Health Secrets
ep27-bio-hack-gut-health.description: The latest science on gut health and why the biohacking community is obsessed with it. Practical tips backed by research, not hype.

ep28-kirill-kimi-founder-just-dropped-40.title: Kimi Founder's 40-Minute AI Masterclass
ep28-kirill-kimi-founder-just-dropped-40.description: The founder of Kimi drops a masterclass on building AI products — from founding principles to scaling, and why the best AI companies are built differently.

ep29-matt-pocock-two-new-skills-this-wee.title: Matt Pocock's New Skills: Handoff and Beyond
ep29-matt-pocock-two-new-skills-this-wee.description: Matt Pocock introduces two new AI-powered skills this week — including Handoff, a tool that changes how developers work with AI agents on complex codebases.

ep30-dunik-40-code-claude-writes-you-was.title: 40% of Your Code — Claude Writes It and You Wasted Your Time
ep30-dunik-40-code-claude-writes-you-was.description: A look at how much code AI is actually writing in production environments, and whether developers are wasting time fighting it instead of leveraging it.

ep31-bio-hack-gut-health.title: Gut Health: The Bio Hack Everyone's Talking About
ep31-bio-hack-gut-health.description: Why gut health has become the central focus of the biohacking movement, and what the science actually says about probiotics, microbiome diversity, and longevity.

ep32-en-wehrman-this-new-flat-earth-conc.title: A New Flat Earth Conceptual Model — and Why It Matters
ep32-en-wehrman-this-new-flat-earth-conc.description: We examine a new conceptual model for the flat earth theory — not to endorse it, but to understand why these ideas persist and what they reveal about how people process information.

ep38-matt-pocock-grill-me-my-most-popula.title: Matt Pocock's Grill with Docs: AI Pair Programming Evolved
ep38-matt-pocock-grill-me-my-most-popula.description: Matt Pocock's most popular skill 'Grill Me' got an upgrade. By combining relentless AI interviewing with Domain-Driven Design's Ubiquitous Language concept, 'Grill with Docs' creates a shared vocabulary that makes AI-assisted coding faster, more precise, and less repetitive.

ep39-how-run-paperclip-hermes-24-hours.title: How to Run Paperclip and Hermes in 24 Hours
ep39-how-run-paperclip-hermes-24-hours.description: Julian Goldie explains how to connect Hermes agents to Paperclip's operating layer — turning isolated chatbots into a managed AI team with roles, tickets, reporting, and real workflow structure.

ep40-movez-anthropic-head-product-just-d.title: Anthropic Head of Product's 28-Minute AI Masterclass
ep40-movez-anthropic-head-product-just-d.description: Anthropic's Head of Product dropped a masterclass on building with AI — practical insights from inside the company behind Claude on product strategy, agent design, and what actually works.

ep41-maxinomics-heres-full-video-why-sma.title: Why a Small Town in North Carolina Is America's Chip Ace in the Hole
ep41-maxinomics-heres-full-video-why-sma.description: Maxinomics explains why China will always depend on the US for chips — and how one small town in North Carolina holds the key to America's semiconductor dominance.

ep42-vincent-logic-信号噪音-未来的世界属于懂-token-的.title: The 10-Year-Old Who Understands AI Tokens Better Than Most Experts
ep42-vincent-logic-信号噪音-未来的世界属于懂-token-的.description: A 10-year-old Chinese blogger explains why tokens are the hard currency of the AI era, breaks down the AI supply chain from energy to applications, and runs multiple AI agents on his new Mac Studio. His insights on compute and token economics might be closer to the truth than many expert reports.

ep43-airbnb-engineers-agentic-coding-pro.title: Airbnb Engineers on Agentic Coding in Production
ep43-airbnb-engineers-agentic-coding-pro.description: Two senior staff engineers from Airbnb explain how they shipped one of the most ambitious LLM-agent migrations in production — live lecture on real agentic coding workflows that actually ship.

ep44-best-claude-cowork-tutorial-under-2.title: The Best Claude Cowork Tutorial Under 25 Minutes
ep44-best-claude-cowork-tutorial-under-2.description: Tina Huang, ex-Meta data scientist, delivers the definitive Claude Cowork walkthrough — from setup to advanced workflows in under 25 minutes.

ep45-guarani-language-soul-of-paraguay.title: Guaraní: The Indigenous Language That Outlived an Empire
ep45-guarani-language-soul-of-paraguay.description: Why Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where an indigenous language is spoken by the majority — and how Guaraní became the heartbeat of a nation.

ep46-chipa-and-terere-taste-of-paraguay.title: Chipa and Tereré: The Taste of Paraguay
ep46-chipa-and-terere-taste-of-paraguay.description: How a simple cheese bread and a cold herbal drink became Paraguay's most iconic cultural rituals — UNESCO-recognised, legally protected, and impossible to imagine life without.

ep47-paraguay-war-that-almost-erased-a-n.title: The War That Almost Erased Paraguay From the Map
ep47-paraguay-war-that-almost-erased-a-n.description: The War of the Triple Alliance killed up to seventy percent of Paraguay's men and lost forty percent of its territory. How one nation survived near-extinction and rebuilt itself.

ep48-polka-paraguaya-music-of-resilience.title: Polka Paraguaya: How a European Dance Became a National Anthem
ep48-polka-paraguaya-music-of-resilience.description: Paraguay took the European polka and made it something entirely its own — a UNESCO-recognised musical tradition built on Guaraní soul, Paraguayan harp, and the resilience of a people who refused to stop singing.

ep49-welsh-migrants-paraguay.title: The Welsh Who Chose Paraguay
ep49-welsh-migrants-paraguay.description: In the 1880s, a group of Welsh settlers crossed the Atlantic to build a New Wales in the heart of South America. Two wounded cultures — Wales stripped of autonomy, Paraguay stripped of its population — found each other and built something unexpected.

ep50-flight-attendant-top-hacks-save-big.title: Flight Attendant's Top Hacks to Save Big on Flights
ep50-flight-attendant-top-hacks-save-big.description: An ex-flight attendant shares four insider tricks: the best days to book, why incognito mode matters, which days are cheapest to fly, and the service that automatically refunds you when prices drop after booking.

ep51-khairallah-al-awady-anthropics-clau.title: Building an AI Agent With Real Memory — From Anthropic's Claude Team
ep51-khairallah-al-awady-anthropics-clau.description: Anthropic's Claude team shows how to build an AI agent with persistent memory in under 30 minutes. Free, practical, and from the people who built Claude.

ep53-godfather-ai-lecture-that-keeps-you.title: The Godfather of AI: The Lecture That Keeps You Awake
ep53-godfather-ai-lecture-that-keeps-you.description: If you sleep well tonight, you may not have understood this lecture. A 47-minute deep dive into the state of AI from one of its pioneers — covering why everything is about to change and what it means for everyone.

ep55-paraguays-bloody-independence.title: Paraguay's Bloody Independence
ep55-paraguays-bloody-independence.description: What would you do if I told you that one of the bloodiest wars in modern history was fought in a small landlocked country in the heart of South America — and that this catastrophe was the direct legacy of a fight for independence that began more than half a century earlier? A special Independence Day episode tracing Paraguay's bloody path from 1811 to the War of the Triple Alliance.

ep57-nous-research-hermes-agent-v0140-fo.title: Hermes Agent v0.14: The Foundation Release
ep57-nous-research-hermes-agent-v0140-fo.description: Nous Research drops the biggest Hermes Agent update yet — version 0.14, dubbed The Foundation Release. GROC 4.3 now supports a 1 million token context window, one-click installation arrives via agent client protocol registry, and nine new optional skills join the platform including Yahoo Finance, Notion, and API testing. With 22 messaging platforms now supported and native Windows support in early beta, this is the release that makes Hermes a foundation for serious agent work.

ep58-rahul-boris-cherny-creator-claude-c.title: Boris Cherny on Claude Code: 4% of All GitHub Commits and Counting
ep58-rahul-boris-cherny-creator-claude-c.description: The creator of Claude Code reveals that 4% of all GitHub commits are now written by his tool — heading toward 20% by year's end. In this deep dive, Boris Cherny explains why he built Claude Code as a terminal hack that nobody initially liked, how Anthropic's engineering team achieved 200% productivity gains per engineer, and why the printing press is the best analogy for what AI coding is about to do to software development.

ep59-shocking-deal-saved-clarity-act-gol.title: Goldman Sachs and Citadel Are Buying XRP — Here's Why It Matters
ep59-shocking-deal-saved-clarity-act-gol.description: Citadel increased its XRP position by 63 percent and closed all put hedges. Goldman Sachs holds nearly two million shares in Bitwise's XRP ETF. Italy's largest bank is buying through Grayscale. Meanwhile the Clarity Act has a 67 percent chance of becoming law, Nasdaq is planning tokenized equities, and JP Morgan's JPM Coin is already running on public blockchain. The institutional flood into crypto is no longer a prediction — it's happening right now.

ep60-muhammad-shehada-this-short-film-ex.title: What the Founding Fathers of Israel Actually Said Behind Closed Doors
ep60-muhammad-shehada-this-short-film-ex.description: Historical documents and statements from Israel's own founding figures paint a more complicated picture than the standard narrative suggests. Ben-Gurion called partition a temporary strategy. Weizmann said it would only last 25 to 30 years. Accounts of the 1948 conflict include allegations of deliberate provocation, systematic brutality, and whisper propaganda designed to spread fear. The same patterns of contested narratives and resistance to scrutiny echo into the present, shaping how we see the conflict today.

ep61-avid-peter-steinberger-creator-open.title: Peter Steinberger's 9 Rules for Agentic Engineering
ep61-avid-peter-steinberger-creator-open.description: Peter Steinberger, creator of OpenClaw, shares his 9 rules for working with AI coding agents — from the Agent Trap curve to empathy for agents, context management, running multiple agents simultaneously, and the Soul.MD concept. A masterclass in treating AI agents as capable engineers while adding the human creativity and vision that machines still can't replicate.

ep62-hermes-goal-command-essential-agent.title: Hermes Goal Command: Make Your AI Agent Finish the Job
ep62-hermes-goal-command-essential-agent.description: The Hermes Goal command gives your AI agent a persistent objective that loops automatically until achieved — judged by an auxiliary model with a configurable turn budget and full session persistence. We break down how it works, the subgoal system for tightening criteria mid-flight, and nine other essential slash commands including cron scheduling, background processing, branch forking, and rollback safety that together transform Hermes from a chat interface into a complete AI agent operating system.

ep63-movez-microsoft-senior-ai-developer.title: Microsoft's AI Agents with Claude: Build, Connect, Ship
ep63-movez-microsoft-senior-ai-developer.description: A Microsoft Senior AI developer demonstrates how to build production-ready AI agents using Claude Opus 4.7 inside Microsoft Foundry. The platform supports over 1,400 built-in connectors and MCP tools, with enterprise security, observability, and governance baked in. From environment setup to a working cupcake store agent that handles customer registration, flavour selection, and order fulfilment — a practical walkthrough of the full agent development lifecycle.

ep64-spotify-chief-architect-how-they-sh.title: Spotify's Chief Architect: 4,500 Deployments a Day with AI
ep64-spotify-chief-architect-how-they-sh.description: Spotify's Chief Architect reveals how they ship 4,500 deployments daily using AI. With 99% of engineers using AI coding tools and 2.5 million automated maintenance PRs merged, the company built Honk — an AI agent powered by Claude that handles complex migrations at scale. From Fleet Management to the Golden State standardisation framework and Backstage developer portal, this episode breaks down the infrastructure, tools, and principles behind one of the most impressive AI-powered engineering operations in the world.

ep65-exploring-worlds-largest-100-billio.title: The $100 Billion Ghost City Nobody Moved To
ep65-exploring-worlds-largest-100-billio.description: Forest City in Malaysia was built for a million people across four man-made islands. Today, fewer than ten thousand residents live there while the developer carries $190 billion in debt. A cautionary tale of property bubbles, government crackdowns, and one experimental community trying to breathe life into empty towers using Balaji Srinivasan's Network State concept.

ep65-this-home-costs-300-build-0-heat-fo.title: This Home Costs $300 to Build and $0 to Heat FOREVER. Why Is It Banned?
ep65-this-home-costs-300-build-0-heat-fo.description: Adobe — just mud, sand, and straw — outperforms modern construction in strength, insulation, and cost, yet it's been systematically excluded from building codes for nearly a century. Each brick costs three cents, walls maintain stable temperatures without any mechanical system, and a University of Arizona study showed adobe homes needed zero cooling while wood-frame homes ran air conditioning ten months a year. The codes were written by the Portland Cement Association, an $18 billion industry protecting its market. But legal loopholes exist, and Simone Swan used them to build 600 adobe homes for families earning under $12,000 a year — with zero energy bills and no mortgage.

ep66-kol415-commentary-larken-rose-ip-wr.title: Kinsella vs Rose: The Libertarian Civil War Over Intellectual Property
ep66-kol415-commentary-larken-rose-ip-wr.description: Stefan Kinsella dissects Larken Rose's arguments against intellectual property — and finds Rose guilty of the very hypocrisy he denounces. Rose opposes copyright on principle, yet issued DMCA takedowns when his own film was pirated. Kinsella argues that property rights only apply to scarce, rivalrous resources, that creation itself does not confer ownership, and that once information escapes into the world, third parties have no contractual obligation to its creator. A philosophical cage match between two libertarians who agree on almost everything except this.

ep67-narcissist-state-groundbreaking-psy.title: The Narcissist State: A Psychological Perspective on Statism
ep67-narcissist-state-groundbreaking-psy.description: What if the State operates not through ideology but through the precise dynamics of narcissistic abuse? Philip Bodessell, a UK barrister imprisoned for refusing COVID masking, maps family roles like Golden Child, Enabler, and Scapegoat onto political structures and identifies mechanisms like Gaslighting, DARVO, and Intermittent Reinforcement in statecraft. The framework is structural, not conspiratorial, and aims to give people a compass and map for concrete exit strategies rather than abstract philosophical arguments.

ep68-complete-guide-building-skills-clau.title: The Complete Guide to Building Skills for Claude
ep68-complete-guide-building-skills-clau.description: Anthropic's official guide to building Agent Skills for Claude — from the three-level progressive disclosure system and YAML frontmatter requirements to five battle-tested patterns for workflow orchestration, multi-MCP coordination, iterative refinement, context-aware tool selection, and domain-specific intelligence. Whether you are a developer building standalone skills or enhancing an MCP integration, this episode covers everything from planning and testing to distribution and troubleshooting.

ep69-mises-media-system-designed-not-be-.title: Mises Media: Rothbard's Political Strategy as Entrepreneurship
ep69-mises-media-system-designed-not-be-.description: After Thomas Massie's defeat in the most expensive House primary in U.S. history, the Mises Institute panel discusses what went wrong and what libertarians should do next. Ryan McMaken, Connor O'Keeffe, and Tho Bishop explore how Rothbard treated political strategy as entrepreneurship — with scarce time and resources governed by opportunity cost. They question the value of libertarian congressmen in modern DC, examine the generational divide between young Massie supporters and older Fox News viewers, and propose alternative approaches including state-level activism and building special interest groups for liberty.

ep70-video-agenticengineering.title: Why AI Agents Are Switching from Markdown to HTML
ep70-video-agenticengineering.description: An Anthropic cloud code engineer argues that HTML is becoming a superior interface for AI agents compared to markdown. As agents generate richer content — SVG diagrams, interactive controls, animated prototypes, and custom editors — plain text can no longer carry the weight of what agents need to communicate. The bottleneck is no longer code generation speed but the interface through which humans stay cognitively connected to what agents produce.

ep33-ronin-andrej-karpathy-90-your-ai-co.title: Andrej Karpathy: 90% of Your AI Coding Bill is Wasted
ep33-ronin-andrej-karpathy-90-your-ai-co.description: Andrej Karpathy breaks down how most AI coding costs come from inefficient prompt patterns and redundant iterations. Practical strategies to cut your AI development spend dramatically while getting better results.

ep34-matt-pocock-anthropic-has-given-us-.title: Matt Pocock: Anthropic Has Given Us a Dedicated Monthly Budget
ep34-matt-pocock-anthropic-has-given-us-.description: Matt Pocock reveals how Anthropic is providing dedicated monthly budgets for power users of Claude Code, and what this means for the future of AI-assisted development workflows.

ep35-how-build-obsidian-vault-that-runs-.title: How to Build an Obsidian Vault That Runs Your Entire Life
ep35-how-build-obsidian-vault-that-runs-.description: A comprehensive guide to setting up Obsidian as a personal knowledge management system that handles everything from daily planning to long-term projects and knowledge capture.

ep36-hermes-agent-masterclass-akshay-pac.title: Hermes Agent Masterclass with Akshay Pachaar
ep36-hermes-agent-masterclass-akshay-pac.description: Akshay Pachaar walks through building production-grade AI agents with the Hermes framework, covering architecture patterns, tool integration, and deployment strategies.

ep37-building-local-knowledge-base-herme.title: Building a Local Knowledge Base with Hermes Agent, Obsidian, and LLM
ep37-building-local-knowledge-base-herme.description: A step-by-step tutorial on creating a fully local knowledge base using the Hermes agent framework, Obsidian for storage, and local LLMs for processing — no cloud services required.

ep70-history-london-docklands-from-roman.title: The History of London Docklands: From Roman Port to Canary Wharf
ep70-history-london-docklands-from-roman.description: A journey through two thousand years of London's Docklands — from the Roman port of Londinium and the chaotic medieval riverfront, through the explosive growth of the enclosed docks during the British Empire, the devastation of the Blitz, the decline and dereliction brought by containerisation, and the dramatic Canary Wharf regeneration that transformed derelict warehouses into one of the world's great financial districts.

ep71-microsoft-cancels-internal-anthropi.title: Microsoft Cancels Internal Anthropic Contract
ep71-microsoft-cancels-internal-anthropi.description: Microsoft cancelled an internal pilot giving staff access to Anthropic's Claude Code after token-based billing blew through the budget in months. Uber burned its entire 2026 AI budget by April. AI software prices surged 20-37%. GitHub abandoned flat-rate plans. When a company with infinite cloud resources decides a third-party AI tool is too expensive, something fundamental is broken in enterprise AI pricing.

ep72-santiago-step-step-video-build-voic.title: Build a Voice Agent From Scratch with AssemblyAI and Claude Code
ep72-santiago-step-step-video-build-voic.description: AssemblyAI's Voice Agent API handles the hard parts of building conversational AI — turn detection, interruptions, speech-to-text and back again — all in a single unified API. Pair it with Claude Code and an MCP server that gives the agent real-time access to documentation, and you can build a fully conversational voice agent in minutes. Santiago walks through the entire process step by step.

ep73-blackheath-greenwich-park-walk-thro.title: Blackheath and Greenwich Park: A Walk Through 2000 Years of History
ep73-blackheath-greenwich-park-walk-thro.description: A vivid walk through two millennia of Blackheath and Greenwich Park — from the Roman road and temple remains, through Saxon settlements and medieval rebellions, Tudor royal hunting grounds and the Palace of Placentia, the Royal Observatory and the birth of GMT, the oldest golf club in England, plague burials, Chartist and suffragette rallies on the heath, the Victorian railway transformation, WWII bombing devastation, and modern conservation of one of London's most historic green spaces.

ep74-borough-market-1000-years-london-pl.title: Borough Market: 1000 Years of London on a Plate
ep74-borough-market-1000-years-london-pl.description: From Roman merchants haggling over salted fish beneath the first London Bridge to Instagram influencers photographing artisan doughnuts beneath Victorian railway arches, Borough Market has been continuously reinventing itself for a millennium. This episode traces the market through medieval charters and Shakespeare's Southwark, the great wholesale golden age, near-death by supermarket, and the 1990s foodie renaissance led by Neal's Yard Dairy, Brindisa, and Monmouth Coffee — plus its starring roles in Bridget Jones, Harry Potter, and Lock, Stock.
